output.summary: Anthropic closed its initial public offering of 1,127,000,000 Class A shares at $83.00 per share, including the underwriters' full option, for gross proceeds of approximately $93.5 billion, of which approximately $91.6 billion went to Anthropic; the stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. It also closed a concurrent private placement of 313,253,007 Class N shares, at the same price and for approximately $26.0 billion, with Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron Technology, Microsoft, NVIDIA and TSMC Partners.
output.relevance: Observed: a frontier-model developer now raises capital in public markets, and seven named technology companies bought a separate class of its equity at the same time. Inference: that couples the company's financing more closely to the companies it works with, but the retrieved documents do not say what rights Class N shares carry or why the purchasers bought them.
evidenceQualifications: All figures come from Anthropic's own press releases; no registration statement, prospectus or independent report was retrieved.
The rights attached to the Class N shares are not described in the retrieved documents.
Proceeds are gross, before underwriting discounts, commissions and expenses.
output.selectionRationale: Largest and most consequential capital event in the window, with a structural feature (a concurrent placement to seven technology companies) that bears on how frontier development is financed.
